skill.description: Build process-based discrete-event simulations in Python with SimPy for queues, resources, events, and monitoring.

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by SimPy resource.request, self.env, Markdown backticks, and ordinary simulation terms. The confirmed issue is CSV export code that writes to caller-supplied filenames, which can overwrite local files. No evidence found of network calls, shell command execution, credential access, or prompt-injection instructions to bypass security review.

remediation.issue: CSV export writes to caller-supplied filenames.
remediation.suggestion: Limit exports to user-approved paths, add overwrite confirmation, and document that export creates local files.

remediation.issue: Runtime instructions promote an external K-Dense service.
remediation.suggestion: Move the K-Dense Web recommendation to marketplace metadata or remove it from runtime skill instructions.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable models for queues, resources, and timed processes before changing real systems. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured SimPy guidance, templates, and monitoring patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains SimPy environments, generator processes, events, and simulation time.
Shows resource, priority resource, preemptive resource, container, and store patterns.
Provides queue, producer-consumer, and parallel task examples.
Includes monitoring helpers for utilization, queue length, wait time, and CSV export.
Covers process signaling, interrupts, real-time environments, and validation practices.
limitations: It does not install SimPy or Python dependencies.
It is not designed for continuous ODE models or pure optimization.
Examples need domain parameters before results are meaningful.
CSV export writes to the filename supplied by the caller.

use_cases.title: Model Service Queues
use_cases.description: Estimate wait times, utilization, and throughput for desks, clinics, or call centers.

use_cases.title: Plan Resource Capacity
use_cases.description: Compare staffing, machine, or server capacity before committing to operational changes.

use_cases.title: Simulate Process Coordination
use_cases.description: Prototype packet flow, scheduling, or workflow behavior before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Queue
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a SimPy model for a single service queue. Include arrivals, service time, one resource, and the metrics to collect.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a basic queueing model.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Resource Capacity
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an experiment that compares two, three, and four resources for the same arrival stream. Report utilization, wait time, and throughput.

prompt_templates.title: Add Monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my SimPy model with resource monitoring for queue length, utilization, and wait time. Explain where each metric is recorded.

prompt_templates.title: Model Interrupts and Priorities
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this process design and propose a SimPy approach using priority resources, interrupts, and validation checks for deadlocks.

output_examples.input: A clinic wants to compare one triage nurse with two triage nurses.
output_examples.output: A model plan with patients, triage nurses, arrivals, service times, wait-time metrics, and a capacity comparison.

output_examples.input: A factory line needs to track machine utilization and queue length.
output_examples.output: A monitoring approach that records each request and release, then summarizes utilization and maximum queue length.

output_examples.input: A network team wants to simulate priority packet handling.
output_examples.output: A priority resource design with normal and urgent packets, preemption rules, and validation checks.

best_practices: Define entities, resources, processes, and metrics before writing the model.
Use resource context managers and yield every SimPy event.
Set random seeds and validate simple cases against expected behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not use blocking sleep calls inside SimPy processes.
Do not reuse events after they have already been triggered.
Do not collect only final state when queue dynamics matter.

faq.question: What is SimPy used for?
faq.answer: SimPy models systems where processes compete for resources over simulated time.

faq.question: Does this skill run simulations by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and helper scripts for Python SimPy projects.

faq.question: Can it model priority queues?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers PriorityResource and PreemptiveResource patterns for priority and interruption behavior.

faq.question: Can it export results?
faq.answer: Yes. The monitoring helper can export CSV data to a caller-supplied filename.

faq.question: Is it suitable for continuous simulation?
faq.answer: No. Use ODE or numerical solvers for continuous systems with fixed time steps.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare arrival patterns, service distributions, resource limits, and the metrics you need.
